newsitem.title: SYRIA: Syria media praises Albright on land-for-peace.
newsitem.headline: Syria media praises Albright on land-for-peace.

text.p: Syrian newspapers on Saturday praised U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright's remarks that Middle East peace should be based on land-for-peace and urged Washington to play the role of the honest broker.
Official newspapers, ahead of a visit by peace envoy Dennis Ross to the region, said Washington should pressure Israel to hand back occupied Arab lands to revive the battered peace process.
"The remarks are a step in the right direction," the official daily al-Thawra said.
"Albright's remarks are important because they bring back to mind the real essence of peace, and at the same time they confirm the U.S. commitment to just and comprehensive peace."

Albright said on Wednesday: "We seek a just and lasting peace achieved through direct negotiations, based on U.N. Security Council resolutions 242 and 338, including the principle on which every Arab-Israeli agreement has been built: land for peace."

The Ross visit also coincides with a flare-up on the border between Israel and Lebanon. Israeli planes rocketed on Saturday a Hizbollah training camp in the Syrian-policed Bekaa Valley close to the Syrian borders, Lebanese security sources said.
Palestinian President Yasser Arafat on Saturday accused Israel of waging "state terrorism" against his people as punishment for a double suicide bombing in a Jewish market in Jerusalem.
Addressing an emergency session of the Palestinian legislature hours before Ross was due back in the region, Arafat said:

"We are committed to peace, to the peace of the brave, not the peace of dictation, orders, starvation and siege. Our people will not kneel," he said, referring to Israel's closure of the West Bank and Gaza Strip after the July 30 twin blasts.
The U.S.-sponsored Arab-Israeli peace talks opened in Madrid in 1991, based on the land-for-peace principle.

Sporadic Syrian-Israeli peace talks ground to a halt when Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, elected in 1996, rejected withdrawal from the Golan Heights, captured from Syria in 1967. Syria demands full withdrawal.
The English language daily Syria Times said Syria wants an agreement that could ensure the full return of the Golan Heights. It said a U.S. decision was required to solve the Middle East crisis.
"Syria asks for a full and comprehensive agreement that could not be subject to future negotiations," it said.
The official newspapers also condemned Israel's attacks on Lebanon, calling on Arabs and the international community to show solidarity with Lebanon.
"It is time that efforts were met to save south Lebanon from Israel's aggression," the Tishreen daily said.

"As long as Israel dismisses all calls to stop its aggressive and provocative practices...then it is the right and the duty of the Lebanese people to continue resisting occupation," it said in reference to attacks on Israeli troops by Lebanese guerrillas.
